title: Tool-call gate before execution
text: Right before an agent runs a tool or a shell command, turn the command into a few narrow yes/no questions and a risk score, and let code decide to allow it, ask a person, or block it.

title: Completion-claim check at stop
text: When an agent is about to stop and says the work is done, judge whether that claim matches the evidence in the session, and send the agent back to work when it does not.

title: Rule-by-target violation scan
text: Ask one plain-language rule as a yes/no question of every file, line, code fragment or paragraph, and return a list of violation probabilities plus an exit code.

title: Diff and pull request review verdicts
text: Turn a code change (diff, pull request or issue) into a small number of narrow judgments that produce a pass, review or block verdict and a list of places to review.

title: Input and output guardrails for LLM apps and MCP
text: Judge text passing through an LLM app, MCP server or gateway for prompt injection, data leaks, harmful content or personal data, and pass, review or block it.

title: Feed and chat content filtering
text: Judge posts, comments and messages written by people as spam, advertising, machine-written text, clickbait or spoilers, and collapse, blur or delete them.

title: Context and tool-output pruning
text: Instead of generating a summary, ask of each old tool call, tool result or log fragment whether it is still needed, and drop or shorten the ones that are not.

title: Memory selection, recall and validation
text: Decide per memory item whether an agent should store it, bring it back for the current turn, or still trust it.

title: Model and reasoning-effort router
text: Judge the difficulty, risk and type of each request or turn, and pick which model, reasoning effort or execution mode handles it.

title: Skill, tool and agent selection
text: From the installed skills, tools, MCP servers or agents, pick the one to use for the current step, or none.

title: Ticket, mail and request triage
text: Judge each incoming ticket, email, issue or form on type, urgency and owner with parallel questions, and route it to a queue or a handler.

title: Single text classification or score
text: The simplest classifier: attach one label or one score to one piece of text.

title: Multi-axis questions combined into a scorecard
text: Split the evaluation of one target into several narrow questions asked in parallel, and let code combine the answers with thresholds and weights into a score, a grade or a verdict.

title: Confidence-threshold cascade and fallback
text: Use the confidence of a Jev answer to choose between acting automatically, escalating to a larger model, and sending the case to a person.

title: Candidate rerank
text: Add a relevance or fit judgment for each candidate in a list made by another system (keyword search, embeddings, an LLM), then reorder the list or keep only the top.

title: Exhaustive semantic scan
text: With no candidate list, ask one natural-language condition of every line, function or file in a codebase or document set, and return the locations that match.

title: Extraction by pointing at numbered fragments
text: Jev cannot write, so have it pick the number or label of a source fragment; code then copies the original text out or fills in a blank with it.

title: Output built from repeated choices
text: Produce something that seems to need generation by repeating or assembling choices, one character, token or field at a time.

title: Generator model plus Jev judge
text: Another language model writes the text or the action values; Jev only judges the approach, whether to accept, the ranking or the quality.

title: Browser next-action loop
text: Convert a web page into a numbered table of its elements; at every step Jev picks the operation and the target element, and code performs it.

title: Desktop, mobile and voice control loop
text: Convert the screen of a desktop or phone app, or a spoken command, into a list of candidate actions; Jev picks one and code performs it.

title: Real-time game control per tick
text: On every tick, code converts the game or simulation state into text or a list of candidate moves and Jev picks the action, at rates from a few to sixty times a second.

title: One move per turn in board games and puzzles
text: On every turn of a game such as chess, gomoku, 2048 or minesweeper, pick one move from the list of legal moves.

title: Simulated characters and NPCs
text: For each simulated person (villager, NPC, panel member), decide actions and reactions with judgments, and add them up into a group outcome.

title: Robot, vehicle, drone and traffic control
text: Turn sensor or simulator state into a short scene description with classic vision and code, and let Jev pick the maneuver or tactic that moves the physical system.

title: Trading and market judgments
text: Convert market state (order book, chart, news) into text and judge buy, sell or hold, or the probability of a direction; code places the orders.

title: Supervisor alongside a coding agent
text: The working agent keeps going while Jev judges, after each step, whether it is finished or stuck and whether the next step is fix, verify, replan or ask a person.

title: Judgments as SQL, CLI and batch primitives
text: Make a Jev judgment callable from an existing system: an SQL function, a shell command, a pipe stage or a large batch job.

title: Local imitations and compatible servers
text: Servers, models and training methods that imitate a Jev call with open models: an endpoint compatible with /v1/systemone and probabilities from a single forward pass.

title: Jev versus LLM benchmarks
text: Give the same judgment task to Jev and to a language model or another judge, and measure accuracy, speed and cost side by side.

title: Calibration, noise and agreement measurement
text: Measure whether Jev's probabilities match how often it is right, how much they vary between runs, and at which threshold they are safe to act on.

title: Domain test benches
text: Measure Jev on one specific task such as exams, law, finance, chess or review labeling, or use it to score logs of such a task.

title: Tools that design questions and replace LLM calls
text: Meta tools that find the judgments inside existing LLM prompts or workflows that could move to Jev, write the questions, and lint or generate them.

title: No stated mechanism
text: Entries that do not say how they use Jev judgments: explainers, articles, lists, or SDKs without a mechanism of their own.

title: Other one-off designs
text: Single designs that fit none of the other families.
